items.headline: What we know so far after Krakow gun attack
items.blurb: Six people were killed in a random shooting in the city's main square, and three bodies were later found at the home of the attacker.
items.text: At least six people were killed and more than a dozen others injured when a gunman suspected to have ties to the far-right opened fire in central Krakow, the second largest city in Poland. Three bodies were found at his home when it was searched by police. Here is everything we know so far. The attack began shortly before 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) in Krakow's Main Market Square, the bustling central point of the city which is popular with tourists. Police said a man drove into the square before beginning to fire "at random people from his car". Footage from the scene shows scenes of panic as people fled, with the sound of gunfire clearly heard. A passing tram was shot at during the apparently random attack, shattering windows but no passengers were injured. Armed officers raced to the scene and engaged in a gunfight with the suspect, who was shot within three minutes of the attack beginning, preventing a further massacre, officials said. items.headline: Canary Islands’ El Hierro declares emergency amid migrant, refugee influx
items.blurb: El Hierro asks Spanish government for help after more than 3,300 people arrived on boats since start of November.
items.text: Authorities of El Hierro, one of Spain’s Canary Islands, have declared an emergency and asked the government in Madrid for help after a surge in migrants and refugees arriving on boats. “We are very concerned… by this sharp increase in arrivals,” Alpidio Armas, head of the governing council for El Hierro, one of Europe’s main entry points for migrants and refugees from West Africa, told Spanish television on Saturday. “This is precisely what has led us to declare an emergency in order to ensure a framework of cooperation with higher-level institutions.” More than 3,300 people have arrived on the island in about 30 boats since the start of November, according to local authorities. El Hierro has about 11,400 residents. Officials are seeking temporary accommodation for the new arrivals, while conditions at the island’s hospital have become “undesirable”, Armas said. The situation is “ absolutely unsustainable ”, the Reuters news agency quoted Fernando Clavijo, the regional leader of the Canary Islands, as saying on Friday. items.headline: Kenyan doomsday sect leader jailed for 200 years for murder of 190 children
items.blurb: Paul Mackenzie convicted over deaths of children and one adult after followers were ordered to starve themselves and their families The leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult disasters in recent history.
items.text: Paul Mackenzie convicted over deaths of children and one adult after followers were ordered to starve themselves and their families The leader of a Kenyan doomsday sect has been sentenced to 200 years in prison for the murders of 190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult disasters in recent history. The sentence, comprising 100 years for murder by starvation and 100 years by direct homicide, came two weeks after the court in Kenya’s coastal city of Mombasa found the cult leader guilty of the crimes. Prosecutors said Paul Mackenzie and his Good News International church ran ​a Christian doomsday sect whose members were ordered to starve themselves and their children to death to go to heaven before the world ended. His accomplices threatened and beat victims to ensure they followed his orders. The emaciated bodies were found scattered in shallow graves and dumped in latrines. Some had been buried alive. items.headline: Israel's president tasks opposition leader Eisenkot with forming government
items.blurb: Neither PM Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc nor that of his rival secured a majority in last week's election.
items.text: Israel's president says he will task opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot with forming a new coalition government. Isaac Herzog has been holding talks with political parties after neither Eisenkot's bloc nor that of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu secured a majority in Israel's parliament, known as the Knesset, following last week's election. Eisenkot will now have 28 days to try to form a new administration, with a potential 14-day extension. "Now is the time to form a national emergency government. I will do everything to ensure we are worthy," the former military chief wrote on X. No political party in Israel has ever won an outright majority, meaning all governments have been coalitions. Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party and its far-right and ultra-Orthodox Jewish allies won 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset, while Eisenkot's centrist Yashar party and three other Jewish opposition parties in his bloc won 48. Two Arab-led alliances, the United Arab List and the Joint List, together won an unprecedented 19 seats following a surge in turnout among Arab voters. That positions them as potential kingmakers. items.headline: ANC faces bruising defeat in South African local elections with 80% of ballots counted
items.blurb: Former liberation movement’s share of national vote almost 14 percentage points below 2021 result The African National Congress is on course to suffer a bruising defeat in South Africa’s local elections, with the once dominant party of Nelson Mandela falling to under a third of the vote nationally with more than 80%…
items.text: Former liberation movement’s share of national vote almost 14 percentage points below 2021 result The African National Congress is on course to suffer a bruising defeat in South Africa’s local elections, with the once dominant party of Nelson Mandela falling to under a third of the vote nationally with more than 80% of ballots counted. Wednesday’s fragmented vote marks another stage in the decline of the ANC, which has led national governments since the end of white minority apartheid rule in 1994. High unemployment, crime, corruption and poor local service delivery have all contributed to voters turning away from the party . The former liberation movement is projected to lose its status as the biggest party in the two most populous provinces, Gauteng and KwaZulu-Natal, as parties began coalition negotiations behind closed doors. The final results are expected to be announced on Sunday. The ANC was on 31.8% of the vote nationally, almost 14 percentage points below its 2021 local election result. items.headline: No clear winner after tight New Zealand general election
items.blurb: Weeks of coalition talks could follow after preliminary results pointed to a highly divided national parliament.
items.text: There was no clear winner following New Zealand's election on Saturday, as the leaders of its two major parties preparing for negotiations to form a coalition government. Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's centre-right National Party won 42 seats but was 19 short of the simple majority needed to form a government, despite being the largest party, preliminary results show. Combined with their coalition partners ACT and New Zealand First, they would have a slim lead over the left-leaning bloc if a deal could be reached. But opposition leader Chris Hipkins, whose Labour Party won 36 seats, showed no signs of conceding, saying the "shape of the next government" will remain uncertain "for a while". The tight result followed a campaign shaped by the cost of living and unemployment. Projections show the National Party on 42 seats and Labour on 36. The Greens are on 16, with ACT on 13, New Zealand First on 12, the Opportunity Party on 7 and Te Pāti Māori, which represents Māori interests, on 5. A humanitarian organisation sent the worker to DR Congo to help in the response to the outbreak, which is the second largest on record. items.headline: US offers $20m reward for information about Iran's nuclear programme
items.blurb: Donald Trump has repeatedly raised the prospect of renewing strikes against Iran's nuclear facilities.
items.text: The US has announced a reward of up to $20 million for information about Iran's nuclear programme. The State Department's Rewards for Justice is also offering to potentially relocate the person who provides such details. President Donald Trump claimed last year that Iran's nuclear facilities had been "completely and totally obliterated " following a bombing campaign by the US and Israel. Iran insists its nuclear programme is peaceful and that it has no intention of developing a nuclear weapon. Meanwhile, the US military says it is setting up a task force to enhance Washington's efforts to restrict Iran's movement of weapons and sanctioned material across its borders. The US military's Central Command (Centcom) said Task Force Iron Gate would operate from Tampa, Florida, and would work with other US government agencies. As well as the movement of weapons, it will also focus on dual-use and illegal revenue streams. Centcom estimates that its naval blockade of Iran's ports has prevented the country from exporting more than $25bn in crude oil. items.headline: Punjab Police brings back wanted gangster Gurwinder alias Afridi from Ethiopia
items.blurb: Gurwinder aka Afridi, against whom the Punjab government had announced a reward of ₹5 lakh, landed at Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International (IGI) Airport
items.text: Punjab Police on Sunday brought wanted gangster Gurwinder alias Afridi back to India from Ethiopia. He landed at Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International (IGI) Airport early in the morning and is being escorted to Punjab by a team of the Anti-Gangster Task Force (AGTF). A resident of Tut village in Tarn Taran district, Afridi carries a reward of ₹ 5 lakh announced by the Punjab government . The team escorting him is being led by AGTF SP Bikram Brar, airport sources said. Police sources described the operation as the first instance of Punjab Police securing the return of a fugitive from an African country. The operation comes amid the state police's efforts to track down gangsters who have fled overseas. To strengthen these efforts, Punjab Police has established an Overseas Fugitive Tracking and Extradition Cell (OFTEC) to coordinate with central agencies and foreign law enforcement authorities. Special DGP (AGTF) Parmod Ban and Special DGP (Counter Intelligence) are expected to address a press conference later on Sunday. items.headline: HC restrains unauthorised use of Amitabh’s name, likeness
items.blurb: The Delhi high court has permanently protected the personality rights of veteran Bollywood actor Amitabh Bachchan, restraining entities from using his name, image, voice or other aspects of his persona without his consent
items.text: The Delhi high court has permanently protected the personality rights of veteran Bollywood actor Amitabh Bachchan, restraining entities from using his name, image, voice or other aspects of his persona without his consent. A bench of justice Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav in his November 5 order, decreed the suit filed by Bachchan in 2022 after being informed that he had entered into settlements with four entities, which acknowledged his publicity rights and right to privacy. As part of the settlement, one individual informed the court that he had taken steps to remove the mobile application titled Amitabh Bachchan Video Call, while the other said that it had discontinued publication of its General Knowledge Quizbook, which featured the actor’s image. One individual submitted that it had stopped selling posters bearing Bachchan’s image, name and likeness. Meanwhile, another informed the court that he had deleted the domain name amitabhbachchan.in in November 2022 and had not derived any monetary benefit from it. All four entities undertook not to use Bachchan’s name, image, voice, likeness or any other aspect of his persona in the future

items.headline: Acquitted, but disarmed: SC orders cops to return bodyguard’s revolver
items.blurb: For a private bodyguard, a revolver is more than a weapon — it can be the key to a job
items.text: For a private bodyguard, a revolver is more than a weapon — it can be the key to a job. Mohammad Jamal Mohammad Yunus learnt this the hard way when the police seized his licensed revolver in 2012 in a criminal case, leaving him unable to find work in the very profession he depended on to feed his family. Even after he and seven other accused were acquitted in 2013, the weapon stayed with the authorities, while his plea to get it back languished in court for years. The Supreme Court has now stepped in, ruling that the pendency of an appeal against his acquittal cannot, by itself, justify keeping his revolver away from him indefinitely. Linking the prolonged deprivation of the weapon to its impact on his livelihood, a bench of justices Vikram Nath, R Mahadevan and Aparesh Kumar Singh directed Maharashtra to return it within eight weeks, subject to compliance with the applicable requirements under the Arms Act. items.headline: Costa Rica shell entity and unauthorised foreign transactions - what ED raids at CoinDCX and Delta Exchange found
items.blurb: ED said searches at premises linked to CoinDCX and Delta Exchange uncovered evidence of alleged FEMA violations involving crypto derivatives, tokenised foreign stocks and cross-border transactions. The agency is investigating payments in stablecoins and transfers to overseas affiliates.
items.text: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has revealed that the agency has uncovered evidence for unauthorised international transactions of cryptocurrencies in a series of raids conducted in Bengaluru. According to the ED, the raids were carried out on 4 and 5 November at three premises linked to cryptocurrency platforms CoinDCX and Delta Exchange over allegations of unauthorised cross-border financial transactions in derivative trading in crypto tokens and Real World Asset (RWA) tokens. The investigation was initiated based on information alleging large-scale FEMA violations by Neblio Technologies Private Limited, which operates CoinDCX in India, and Excelium Technologies Private Limited, which operates Delta Exchange. According to the ED, the two platforms were offering products such as derivative trading in crypto tokens, ie. Futures and Options and trading in RWA tokens. These platforms were openly advertising trading in tokenised stocks of foreign entities despite not being authorised to do so. The ED further noted that these platforms were using stablecoins such as USDT to undertake derivative trading and tokenised stock trading in foreign-based crypto trading platforms such as Binance , KuCoin, Gate.io, and Bybit etc.

Aberdeen Investments favors markets powered by stronger domestic growth, including India and Vietnam, and sees upside in Chinese technology firms. Hedge fund Lotus Asset Management is long Hong Kong equity futures, while Allianz Global Investors is looking at healthcare and consumer companies. Asia has been among the hardest hit by the market fallout from the Democrats’ sweep of Congress. items.blurb: Parent company Pop Mart's revenue has fallen as appetite for the quirky collectible monsters wanes.
items.text: Collectors young and old energetically snapped up "blind boxes" - sealed, mystery packages containing the quirky monsters - often paying $15 (£11) or more. Those unable to get the characters they wanted were often prepared to pay much more on the resale market. The hype around the creatures convinced a mega-fan from North Carolina, who goes by the name Ensito, to leave his tech job in 2024 to create Labubu content full-time, travelling as far as Italy and Spain to seek out the latest releases. Ensito has spent more than $50,000 (£37,000) to build his collection of more than 400 Labubus, a figure he tells the BBC he's "embarrassed to say". He even had a row of custom Labubu-like jagged teeth made by a dentist to wear at events. But in recent months, Ensito's once-viral posts about the furry monsters have struggled. "Those videos used to be able to hit 10,000 really quickly but I'm struggling to do that now." Ensito's focus has shifted to other trends like Hello Kitty and squishies. items.text: A sales representative asks an AI agent for customer pricing, and the agent pulls data from multiple sources: restricted pricing systems, internal communications, and archived quotes. The output looks accurate to the agent, so a second agent uses the data to draft the proposal for the sales rep. No human checks either handoff. When it’s discovered that the proposal includes unapproved, confidential, and sensitive information, no one can trace where the problematic data entered the workflow or how it spread across systems, files, and agents. This scenario illustrates why AI governance needs to evolve, rapidly and dynamically. As more enterprises begin to use agentic AI in daily workflows, they’re realizing that they must manage more than static files; they must manage moving and fragmented data that is continuously ingested, copied, summarized, transformed, reused, and redistributed in new forms. In short, AI security isn’t a tool problem; it’s a data visibility problem. Consequently, traditional security approaches built solely around applications, systems, networks, or endpoints are no longer sufficient.
